newsitem.title: USA: Two still at large after escaping Arizona jail.
newsitem.headline: Two still at large after escaping Arizona jail.

text.p: Two more escaped convicts were captured on Sunday but two others eluded police after they fled from a high-security federal prison in Florence, Ariz., police said.
Six inmates in total escaped from the Central Arizona Detention Centre late Saturday or early Sunday by cutting through three layers of fences.

Police apprehended Douglas Armey and Mark Hartdigsen in Phoenix, about 45 miles from Florence, without incident at 9:15 a.m. MDT/11:15 EDT, according to Susan Hart, spokeswoman for the company that owns and operates the facility. Two other escapees were captured around dawn in a home near Florence.

The two still at large "are considered dangerous. They have committed serious offences," said Debbie Argel, a dispatcher at the Florence police department. The two being hunted were convicted of rape and murder.
A seventh inmate was caught trying to escape before he was able to leave the grounds of the prison. The federal prison is privately owned Corrections Corp of America.
Authorities were employing mounted police, a canine squad and a helicopter to search for the two, who are from Alaska, Argel said.
